Édouard Philippe: Prime Minister of France from 2017 to 2020. A lawyer by occupation, Philippe is a former member of the Union for a Popular Movement (UMP), which later became The Republicans (LR).
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henrietta Swan Leavitt (born 1868) is the earliest of the four. Henrietta Swan Leavitt (July 4, 1868 – December 12, 1921) was an American astronomer.
Who among these four was born earliest?

Stephen Gray (scientist) (born 1666) is the earliest of the four. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Which of these four began earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
John Cockcroft is a physicist. Ernest Rutherford accepted Cockcroft as a research student in the Cavendish Laboratory, and Cockcroft completed his doctorate under Rutherford's supervision in 1928.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Dolph Lundgren is a chemist. Hans "Dolph" Lundgren (Swedish: [ˈdɔlːf ˈlɵ̌nːdɡreːn]; born 3 November 1957) is a Swedish-American actor, filmmaker, and martial artist.
What is the atomic number of Unbihexium?
Unbihexium, also known as element 126 or eka-plutonium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has atomic number 126 and placeholder symbol Ubh.
In what year was Steve Jobs born?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
Which company manufactures LTV A-7 Corsair II?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: Ling-Temco-Vought. The LTV A-7 Corsair II is an American carrier-capable subsonic light attack aircraft designed and manufactured by Ling-Temco-Vought (LTV).
In which country is Junkers Ju 52?
Junkers Ju 52: Germany. Development of the Ju 52 commenced in the late 1920s, headed by German aeronautical engineer Ernst Zindel.
Who is credited with discovering Plutonium?
Plutonium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
Who is credited with discovering Fermium?
Fermium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.
Who is credited with discovering Sodium?
Sodium: Humphry Davy. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
With 1,248 built, this turboprop's design was adapted from an earlier Soviet transport aircraft and became NATO's 'Cub' — which four-engine workhorse?
Antonov An-12 (NATO reporting name: Cub) is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Once native to the highland lakes of Xochimilco and Chalco, this neotenic mole salamander keeps its external gills and stays aquatic for life — what is it?
Axolotl (from Classical; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.

The bassist of a legendary British rock band from 1962 to 1993, performing on its first 19 studio albums, this musician was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 as part of that group — who is he?
Bill Wyman (n Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.
This rhythmic bodily process draws oxygen-rich air into the lungs and expels carbon dioxide, powering the cellular chemistry that turns food into energy — what process is it?
Breathing (respiring or ventilating) is the rhythmic process of inhaling air into the lungs providing oxygen, and exhaling the air removing carbon dioxide, in the gas exchange process.
Prized in India for hashish and cultivated from China to West Africa, this Hindu Kush-native plant produces cannabinoid levels well above ordinary hemp — which species?
Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family, this Australian parrot is recognized for its expressive crest and long tail feathers, and is a hugely popular pet bird. What bird is it?

Cockatiel (Nymphicus hollandicus), also known as the weero/weiro or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
This colourless, highly volatile, sweet-smelling organic compound with formula (CH3CH2)2O was once used as a general anesthetic and remains a common laboratory solvent — what is it?
This American physicist was the first to make a transuranium element, neptunium, sharing the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Edwin McMillan (September 18, 1907 - September 7, 1991) was an American physicist credited with being the first to produce a transuranium element, neptunium.

This branch of anthropology systematically studies individual cultures from the point of view of the people within them, relying heavily on researchers directly participating in the settings they study — what is this method called?
Ethnography is a branch of anthropology and the systematic study of individual cultures. It explores cultural phenomena from the point of view of the subject of the study.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive it combines with nearly every other element except the light noble gases. What element is it (symbol F)?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
With the symbol Ge and atomic number 32, this lustrous, brittle metalloid was predicted to exist by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869, decades before it was actually discovered — name this element?
Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is a fisheries staple in northern Europe, often smoked into varieties like Finnan haddie and the Arbroath smokie — what is it?
Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.

This extinct human species from the Middle Pleistocene may represent the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans — or a completely separate lineage altogether — what species is it?
Homo heidelbergensis is a species of archaic human from the Middle Pleistocene of Europe and Africa, as well as potentially Asia depending on the taxonomic convention used.
This Russian-American aviation pioneer, a trailblazer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, won the top prize at the 1912 Moscow Aviation Exhibition for one of his early designs — who is he?
Igor Sikorsky (25 May 1889 - 26 October 1972) was a Russian-American aviation pioneer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
This pain-relieving, fever-reducing drug belongs to the propionic acid class of anti-inflammatories and hit the market in 1980, thirteen years after being patented — what is it?
Ketoprofen is one of the propionic acid class of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) with analgesic and antipyretic effects.
This American computer scientist won the 2013 Turing Award for taming the chaos of distributed systems — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX — who is he?
Leslie Lamport (born February 7, 1941) is an American computer scientist and mathematician.
This paired organ, located near the backbone on either side of the heart in most mammals, extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide back into it — name the organ?
Lung are the primary organs of the respiratory system in many animals, including humans.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.
Carrying NATO's 'Hind' codename and its crews' affectionate 'flying tank,' this Soviet machine is both an attack craft and a low-capacity troop carrier. What is it?
Mil Mi-24 (NATO reporting name: Hind) is a large helicopter gunship, attack helicopter and low-capacity troop transport with room for eight passengers.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.
This American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth bomber, solely operated by the US Air Force, is designed as a flying wing to penetrate sophisticated air defenses. What is this aircraft?
Northrop B-2 Spirit is an American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth strategic bomber, often referred to as a "stealth bomber", solely operated by the United States Air Force.
It surges during childbirth and sexual activity, drives maternal bonding and milk production, and is released by the posterior pituitary — which hormone is this?
Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
This interdisciplinary field studies signs and sign systems, breaking down into branches examining the formal relations between signs, their meanings, and their users — what's the field called?
Semiotics is the study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
This plant family includes both deadly poisonous species and kitchen staples like tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers, all linked by unusually high alkaloid content — what family is it?
Solanaceae is a family of flowering plants in the order Solanales.
In the equation 5 − 2 = 3, this is the operation being performed — which one is it?
Subtraction (which is signified by the minus sign) is one of the four arithmetic operations along with addition, multiplication and division.

This mass of gray matter forming part of the forebrain relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex through radiating nerve fibers, and helps regulate consciousness, sleep, and alertness — what's the structure?
Thalamus (pl.: thalami; from Greek, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter on the lateral wall of the third ventricle forming the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Over 500 of these organic compounds exist in nature, yet only 22 appear in the genetic code, joining together to build proteins — what are they?
Amino acid: Organic compounds containing amine and carboxylic groups.
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2008 for his AIDS-relief work on PEPFAR, this immunologist directed the U.S. allergy and infectious-disease institute from 1984 to 2022. Who is he?
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Sold under the brand name Tessalon, this cough-relief medication works within about 20 minutes by acting as a local anesthetic that blocks stretch receptors in the lungs — what is this drug called?
Benzonatate: Oral cough medication. Benzonatate, sold under the brand name Tessalon among others, is a medication that is used for the symptomatic relief of cough.

Native to North America and classified in the genus Vaccinium, this fruit comes in wild 'lowbush' and cultivated 'highbush' varieties, with Canada leading global production of the wild type — what fruit is it?
Blueberry: Perennial plant with blue berries.
Known for a widely viewed 2010 TEDx talk on shame and vulnerability, which academic wrote six consecutive number-one New York Times bestsellers, including Daring Greatly?
Brené Brown: American academic, speaker and author.
Found in chalk, limestone, eggshells, and pearls alike, this CaCO3 compound is also the active ingredient in agricultural lime and doubles as an antacid — what is it?
Calcium carbonate: Chemical compound. Materials containing much calcium carbonate or resembling it are described as calcareous.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
With independently swiveling eyes, a projectile tongue, and the ability to shift colors, this Old World lizard family is famous for camouflage — which reptile?
Chameleon: Family of reptiles. The members of this family are best known for their distinct range of colours, being capable of colour-shifting camouflage.
This fluoroquinolone antibiotic treats everything from typhoid fever to urinary tract infections but can rarely cause tendon rupture — what drug?
Ciprofloxacin: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Ciprofloxacin, sold under the brand name Cipro among others, is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a number of bacterial infections.
Also known as foremilk or historically as 'beestings,' this early substance produced by mammary glands right after birth delivers antibodies and immune factors to newborns. What is it?
Colostrum: Form of milk produced immediately following the delivery of newborn.
First described in 1880 by a French neurologist, this rare delusion convinces sufferers that they are dead, don't exist, or have lost their internal organs — what is it called?
Cotard's syndrome: Delusion that one is dead or non-existent.
Bred in Germany with short legs and a long body to chase badgers into their burrows, which hound breed comes in smooth-, wire-, and long-haired varieties?
Sold as Voltaren and taken by mouth, suppository, injection, skin gel, or even eye drops, this NSAID eases pain and inflammation like gout for up to eight hours a dose — what is it?
Revered by Ancient Egyptians as the god Khepri for rolling the sun across the sky, which insect feeds exclusively on feces?
Dung beetle: Informal group of insects.
Born in Pretoria and once a Zip2 co-founder, this CEO of Tesla and SpaceX became, by some estimates, the first dollar trillionaire in 2026 — who is he?
Elon Musk: Businessman and public official (born 1971)
Also called moral philosophy, this field splits into normative, applied, and meta- branches as it asks what people ought to do and whether objective moral facts even exist. Which discipline is it?
Birds of prey in the genus Falco, some small species are called hobbies and hover-hunters are called kestrels — what are they collectively known as?
Falcon: Birds of prey in the genus Falco. The largest falcon is the gyrfalcon at up to 65 cm (26 in) in length.
Discovered in Dubna in 1999, this superheavy synthetic element (number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name in Cyrillic explains why its spelling swaps a 'yo' for an 'e' — which element?
Flerovium: Chemical element with atomic number 114 (Fl)
Named in 1753 from Greek words for 'milk' and 'flower,' this genus of about 20 bulbous perennial species is better known by its common name, snowdrop — what is its scientific genus?
Galanthus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Amaryllidacee.

Likely first domesticated by Austronesian peoples in Maritime Southeast Asia, this herbaceous perennial is grown for the spicy rhizome that puts it in the same family as turmeric and cardamom — what is it?
Ginger: Species of plant used as a spice.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.

This English physician co-wrote the first English-language medical textbook on homosexuality in 1897, coined the term 'narcissism,' and penned an early public account of a mescaline trip he took on himself. Who was he?
Havelock Ellis: British physician, eugenicist, writer, and social reformer (1859–1939)
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Teaching philosophy and astronomy in Roman-era Alexandria, this Neoplatonist is considered the first female mathematician whose life is well documented — who is she?
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
This group of three genetic conditions causes nervous-system tumors; its first type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis, while its second causes early hearing loss — what's it called?
Neurofibromatosis: Three genetic disorders involving benign tumors of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Native to western Europe and known scientifically as Ribes rubrum, which widely cultivated berry has escaped into the wild across many regions?
Redcurrant: Flowering plant species in the family Grossulariaceae.
Originating in ancient Rome and used across Europe well into the Late Middle Ages, this numeral system works on which principle?

Roman numerals are a numeral system that originated in ancient Rome and remained the usual way of writing numbers throughout Europe well into the Late Middle Ages. Like many other ancient numeral systems, they are based on the additive principle.
A pharmaceutical chemist with a Dartmouth Ph.D. by day, this American has chaired Anthrocon — one of the world's largest furry conventions — since 1999. Who is he?
Samuel Conway: American chemist and furry fandom personality.
Native to the western slopes of California's Sierra Nevada, this endangered conifer is the largest tree species on Earth, with a record height of 94.8 meters — what is it?
Sequoiadendron giganteum: Species of tree native to North America.
Lose your coiled shell entirely and you're called a slug; keep one big enough to retract into and you're this shelled gastropod instead — what creature?
Snail: Shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
With eight arms plus two extra tentacles for grabbing prey, this soft-bodied mollusc has an internal chitin rod called a gladius instead of a true skeleton — what creature is it?
A sphere of plasma heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion in its core, it radiates mostly visible light and infrared — plus about 10% as what?
The Sun is a massive sphere of hot plasma heated by nuclear fusion in its core, radiating energy mainly as visible light and infrared radiation, with about 10% at ultraviolet energies.
The earliest known example was the stone tool, and the later control of fire is even credited with helping grow the human brain and spark language — what broad field is being described?
Technology: Use of knowledge for practical goals.
Tucked behind the breastbone and in front of the heart, this two-lobed organ is where immature T cells mature, and it's most active before adolescence — which organ?
About 70% of people infected with this parasite-caused sexually transmitted infection show no symptoms at all, though it can raise the risk of contracting HIV — what condition is it?
Trichomoniasis: Medical condition. Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.

Known by names like lingonberry and cowberry, this evergreen shrub's tart berries are a Nordic cuisine staple and are commercially grown in the Pacific Northwest and the Netherlands — what is its scientific name?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea: Species of shrub with edible fruit.
Tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless, this polar molecule's strong hydrogen bonding makes it the solvent inside every known living organism — yet it offers no food energy at all. What is it?
Water: Chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for battling EU-imposed austerity — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis: Greek economist and politician (born 1961)

The symbol for mendelevium is Md. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md and atomic number 101.
What is the chemical symbol for ytterbium?
The symbol for ytterbium is Yb. Ytterbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Yb and atomic number 70.
